Subject: Personal data map + review-window rampdown: action items & comms

Team —

I pulled together a first pass of a personal data map tied to the review cycle (attached). This is intended to be the baseline for:

- what fields we surface to managers during calibration
- which attributes must be redacted from manager packets for sensitive roles
- retention windows and deletion triggers after cycle close

Key asks: please review and respond with your suggestions by EOD Monday (4/26). Specific items I want input on:

1) Redaction rules for privileged roles (HR suggestion needed)
2) Retention timeline we commit to publicly in the manager comms (Legal + Security)
3) Rollback / rampdown criteria if we need to pause the cycle mid-window (ops/runbook)

Attachments: personal-data-map-v1.xlsx, manager_comm_drafts_v2.docx, rampdown-checklist.pdf

I recommend a "quiet launch" to managers on 5/10 with a formal announcement to the org on 5/17, contingent on signoff.

If you prefer a quick sync instead of comments, I'm available today at 4pm PT.

Thanks —
Logan

Head of People Operations (Interim)
Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Personal data map + review-window rampdown: action items & comms

Thanks Logan — quick read-through below. I added inline notes in the sheet and flagged a few manager comm wording tweaks in manager_comm_drafts_v2.docx (see comments tab). Highlights:

- Redaction: For "Privileged - Financial" and "Privileged - Security" roles we should strip: employee Notes, 1:1 feedback excerpts, and any PII beyond name/role until calibration is complete.
- Retention: HR prefers 90 days post-cycle for manager packets to be retained in readable form, then move to archived encrypted storage for 1 year before deletion. We need Legal to confirm compliance with vendor/partner obligations.
- Rampdown triggers: I mapped three immediate triggers — (a) confirmed data exfil event, (b) unresolved legal hold affecting >5% of impacted packets, (c) systemic export bug causing PII leakage. For each trigger we should have a predefined comm path and fallback model (canary fallback to aggregated reports only).

Action items I can take on:
- Draft manager notification with redaction callouts (deliverable: 4/28)
- Owner for packet retention policy doc (I'll shepherd with Legal)

If others agree, we should schedule a 30-min cross-functional lockstep on Monday 4/26 at 10am PT.

—Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior People Ops Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Personal data map + review-window rampdown: action items & comms

Appreciate the thoughtful first pass. A few legal points:

- Retention: 90 days readable + 1 year encrypted archive is reasonable from a risk perspective, but we must add an opt-out/contractual data requirement exception for customers/partners (e.g., Acme's request below).
- Public comms: Do not publish specific redaction thresholds publicly; instead publish the principle ("we limit manager-visible PII for privileged roles") and provide the detailed policy to Audit/Requestors under NDA.
- Rampdown / rollback: Legal wants a hard stop clause when a formal legal hold is issued — this must supersede any operational rampdown. We should bake that into the rampdown-checklist.pdf as an explicit step.

David, can Security confirm whether our current export logs produce a sufficiently granular trail for an immediate forensics request (preferably <5 minutes to pull last 30 days)? If not, we need to postpone quiet launch.

I made a few suggested edits in the Drive doc (link in related_links).

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the heads up and for sharing the data map. Acme Cloud's preference is that any manager packets sent to our account teams remove employee ID numbers and any internal calibration comments until the final calibration step. We can sign an NDA to receive a redacted packet if needed.

A couple practical asks from our side:
- Can you include a short note in the comms to external partners explaining the redaction policy and who to contact for escalations?
- Please confirm the retention window; our procurement team requires a contract clause for any archived personnel data beyond 90 days.

Best,
